questions.q: Which bedside practice is mandatory before a medical student initiates a physical examination on an inpatient?
options: Obtaining explicit verbal consent after introducing oneself and explaining the procedure
Requesting the ward matron to sign a written surgical consent form
Performing an abdominal palpation before washing hands to assess skin temperature
Asking all relatives to remain inside the curtains during an intimate examination
questions.explain: Respect for patient autonomy and bedside etiquette requires introducing oneself, explaining the examination clearly, and obtaining explicit verbal consent before touching the patient.

open.q: What essential communication step must a medical student perform immediately after introducing themselves and before touching a patient for examination?
accept: Explain the procedure and obtain consent

questions.q: According to the WHO Five Moments for Hand Hygiene, when must a clinician perform hand hygiene in relation to aseptic tasks?
options: Only after removing sterile gloves following the procedure
Immediately before performing a clean or aseptic procedure
At the start of the ward round before entering the hospital building
Only when visible blood or body fluid contamination is present
questions.explain: Moment 2 of the WHO Five Moments requires hand hygiene immediately before any clean or aseptic task to protect the patient from harmful organisms entering their body.

open.q: State the exact timing of Moment 2 in the WHO Five Moments for Hand Hygiene regarding clean or aseptic procedures.
accept: Immediately before a clean or aseptic procedure

questions.q: Which member of the hospital multidisciplinary team is primarily responsible for evaluating dysphagia and designing swallowing rehabilitation after an acute ischaemic stroke?
questions.explain: Speech and language therapists assess swallowing mechanics (dysphagia) and communication deficits post-stroke to prevent aspiration pneumonia.

open.q: Which allied health professional assesses swallowing safety and manages dysphagia in patients recovering from a stroke?

questions.q: In the SOAP format of clinical progress notes, where should a patient's newly auscultated bibasal fine inspiratory crackles be recorded?
questions.explain: Objective findings include measurable or observable clinical data obtained by the clinician, such as vital signs, physical examination signs, and laboratory results.

open.q: Under which heading of a SOAP clinical progress note are physical examination findings and vital signs documented?

questions.q: What is the primary distinction between a symptom and a clinical sign?
options: A symptom is experienced and reported by the patient, whereas a sign is elicited or observed by the clinician
A symptom is always pathognomonic of a disease, whereas a sign is non-specific
A symptom appears only in acute illnesses, whereas a sign appears only in chronic illnesses
A symptom is confirmed by laboratory testing, whereas a sign is detected on imaging
questions.explain: Symptoms are subjective experiences reported during history taking (e.g., dyspnoea, chest pain), while signs are objective abnormalities detected on physical examination (e.g., tachypnoea, pedal oedema).

open.q: How does a clinical symptom differ from a clinical sign during patient evaluation?
accept: Symptoms are subjective experiences reported by the patient while signs are objective findings observed by the clinician
Symptom is subjective and sign is objective
Symptoms are felt by the patient and signs are detected on examination

questions.q: Which questioning technique is most appropriate at the beginning of a medical consultation to allow the patient to describe their presenting complaint in their own words?
questions.explain: Open-ended questions (e.g., 'Tell me what brought you to the hospital today') encourage narrative flow and avoid biasing the patient's account early in the interview.

open.q: What type of questioning should a clinician use at the start of a clinical interview to encourage the patient to tell their story freely?

questions.q: In the three-tier structure of the Nigerian public healthcare system, which level of government is primarily statutorily responsible for managing Primary Health Care (PHC) centres?
questions.explain: Nigeria operates a three-tier health system where Local Governments manage Primary Health Care, State Governments manage Secondary (General) Hospitals, and the Federal Government manages Tertiary/Teaching Hospitals.

open.q: Which tier of government in Nigeria holds primary statutory responsibility for Primary Health Care facilities?

questions.q: When a male clinician performs a breast, pelvic, or rectal examination on a female patient, what is the standard professional safeguard?
options: Locking the consultation room door without informing nursing staff
Asking a medical student of the same gender as the doctor to observe alone
Proceeding rapidly without explaining the steps to minimize embarrassment
Ensuring the presence of an impartial trained female chaperone and documenting their identity
questions.explain: Offering and documenting a trained impartial chaperone during intimate examinations protects both the patient's dignity and the clinician against misunderstandings or allegations.

open.q: What safeguard must be provided and documented in the case notes when conducting an intimate physical examination?

questions.q: A 54-year-old man presents with crushing central chest pain radiating to the left arm. Based on pattern recognition, the clinician immediately considers acute myocardial infarction, aortic dissection, and pulmonary embolism before narrowing down via ECG and troponins. Which diagnostic reasoning strategy is being applied?
questions.explain: Hypothetico-deductive reasoning involves generating a targeted shortlist of differential hypotheses early from key cues and testing them systematically through focused history, examination, and investigations.

open.q: Name the clinical reasoning method in which a clinician generates early differential hypotheses from initial cues and tests them systematically.

questions.q: How should an erroneous written entry in a patient's physical hospital case folder be corrected to maintain medico-legal integrity?
options: Cover the mistake completely with white correction fluid
Draw a single line through the error, write the correction, and sign with date and time
Tear out the entire page and rewrite the clerking notes cleanly
Erase the ink with a razor blade so the page looks neat
questions.explain: Altering, obliterating, or removing pages from medical records compromises legal validity; errors must be struck through with a single line so the original text remains legible, dated, and signed.

open.q: What is the proper medico-legal way to correct a written mistake in a paper hospital case note?
accept: Draw a single line through it, sign, and date it
Single line strikethrough with signature and date
Cross it out with one line and initial with date and time

questions.q: Which healthcare team member focuses on helping a patient with residual hemiparesis regain independence in activities of daily living such as dressing, bathing, and feeding?
questions.explain: Occupational therapists adapt tasks and environments to restore functional independence in activities of daily living (ADLs), whereas physiotherapists focus primarily on gross mobility and muscle strength.

open.q: Which rehabilitation specialist helps patients relearn activities of daily living like dressing and feeding after disabling illness?

questions.q: A 28-year-old man newly diagnosed with open pulmonary tuberculosis refuses to inform his household contacts despite counselling. Under medical ethics and public health law, what is the clinician's appropriate action?
options: Publicly display his diagnosis to warn visitors
Notify public health authorities and at-risk contacts, explaining the disclosure
questions.explain: While patient confidentiality is a core duty, justified limited disclosure is ethically and legally required when withholding information poses a serious, preventable risk of harm or infectious transmission to others.

open.q: When is a physician ethically and legally justified in breaching patient confidentiality without consent?
accept: When there is serious risk of harm to others or public health
To prevent serious harm to third parties
When required by law or to protect public safety

questions.q: What does the 'B' stand for in the structured SBAR clinical handover tool?
questions.explain: SBAR stands for Situation, Background, Assessment, and Recommendation, providing a standardized framework for clear interprofessional communication during patient handover or escalation.

open.q: In the SBAR structured clinical handover framework, what do the four letters stand for?

questions.q: Which standard precaution should be taken immediately after performing a venepuncture to prevent needlestick injury?
options: Recap the needle with both hands
Discard the uncapped needle and syringe in a sharps container
Bend the needle tip against a tray
Put the needle in a biohazard bag
questions.explain: Two-handed recapping and bending needles are major causes of needlestick injuries; used sharps must be disposed of immediately at the point of use into a puncture-proof sharps box.

open.q: How should a used venepuncture needle be disposed of immediately after blood collection to prevent needlestick injury?
accept: Place directly into a puncture-resistant sharps container without recapping
Discard uncapped into a sharps box
Dispose directly in a sharps bin

questions.q: In a Nigerian teaching hospital clinical firm, which doctor is a newly graduated medical practitioner undergoing a mandatory one-year supervised rotational clinical training prior to full MDCN registration?
questions.explain: A House Officer (intern) holds provisional registration with the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) and completes a 12-month supervised internship across Medicine, Surgery, Paediatrics, and Obstetrics & Gynaecology.

open.q: What is the title of a newly graduated doctor completing their mandatory 12-month supervised internship for full MDCN registration?

questions.q: In the SPIKES protocol for breaking bad news, what is the primary objective of the 'P' (Perception) step before delivering the diagnosis?
options: Providing a detailed prognosis and chemotherapy schedule
Preparing the physical room and seating arrangements
Permitting the patient to leave the room if overwhelmed
Assessing what the patient already knows or suspects about their medical condition
questions.explain: In SPIKES (Setting, Perception, Invitation, Knowledge, Empathy, Strategy/Summary), assessing the patient's Perception reveals their current understanding and emotional readiness before sharing new information.

open.q: In the SPIKES protocol for breaking bad news, what does the clinician assess during the 'Perception' step?
accept: What the patient already knows or understands about their illness
The patient's current understanding of their condition
How much the patient already knows

questions.q: What is the medical term for an adverse clinical condition or complication caused inadvertently by medical examination, diagnostic procedures, or therapeutic intervention?
questions.explain: Iatrogenic refers to harm or disease resulting from medical treatment or diagnostic intervention (e.g., drug-induced nephrotoxicity or post-lumbar puncture headache), whereas idiopathic means of unknown cause.

open.q: What term describes an unintended adverse effect or illness caused by medical treatment or diagnostic intervention?

questions.q: An infection acquired by a patient during hospital admission that was neither present nor incubating at the time of arrival, typically manifesting 48 hours or more after admission, is termed:
questions.explain: Nosocomial (healthcare-associated) infections develop 48 hours or more after hospital admission and are commonly linked to indwelling catheters, surgical wounds, or poor hand hygiene.

open.q: What is the clinical term for an infection acquired during hospital care that manifests 48 hours or more after admission?

questions.q: While reviewing a drug chart on the medical ward, a student notices an order written as 'Insulin soluble 6 U IV stat'. Why is abbreviating 'units' as 'U' considered a high-risk prescribing error?
options: It indicates subcutaneous rather than intravenous administration
It implies the dose should be given only if blood glucose is below 4 mmol/L
A handwritten 'U' can be misread as a zero, resulting in a tenfold overdose of 60 units
Soluble insulin cannot be administered intravenously in emergencies
questions.explain: Abbreviating 'units' as 'U' is banned in safe prescribing guidelines because '6 U' can easily be misread as '60', causing fatal hypoglycaemia; 'units' must always be written out in full.

open.q: Why must the word 'units' always be written in full rather than abbreviated as 'U' on insulin prescriptions?
accept: U can be misread as zero causing a tenfold overdose

questions.q: From which side of the patient's bed is standard clinical physical examination traditionally performed?
options: The left side of the bed
The right side of the bed
questions.explain: Standard bedside clinical examination is performed from the patient's right side, allowing ergonomic palpation of the liver, spleen, apex beat, and jugular venous pulse.

open.q: Which side of the bed should a clinician stand on when performing a standard bedside physical examination?

questions.q: When taking a history from a patient who speaks only a local Nigerian language that the clinician does not understand, who is the preferred interpreter?
options: A trained medical interpreter or bilingual healthcare worker
Another patient in the waiting area
questions.explain: Trained medical interpreters or neutral bilingual staff ensure accurate translation of clinical terms and preserve patient confidentiality, whereas children or untrained bystanders risk distortion and privacy breaches.

open.q: Who is the most appropriate person to translate when a clinician and patient do not share a common language?

questions.q: During a consultation, a clinician explores a patient's Ideas, Concerns, and Expectations (ICE). What is the primary clinical benefit of eliciting the patient's 'Concerns'?
options: It reveals unspoken fears that the clinician can address
It determines the hospital billing category
It removes the need for laboratory tests
questions.explain: Exploring ICE reveals hidden anxieties (e.g., fearing a headache is a brain tumour) and expectations, improving diagnostic alignment, reassurance, and treatment adherence.

open.q: What does the acronym ICE stand for when exploring a patient's perspective during a consultation?

questions.q: Which clinical procedure requires strict surgical aseptic technique (sterile gloves, sterile gown/drape, and skin antisepsis) rather than simple clean non-sterile gloves?
questions.explain: Lumbar puncture breaches the subarachnoid space around the central nervous system and mandates strict surgical asepsis to prevent iatrogenic bacterial meningitis.

open.q: Why does a diagnostic lumbar puncture require strict surgical asepsis rather than clean non-sterile technique?
accept: To prevent introducing bacteria into the subarachnoid space and causing meningitis
Because it enters the sterile CSF space

questions.q: Which specialist within the hospital health team is primarily consulted to formulate individualized enteral or parenteral nutrition regimens for a malnourished patient with chronic kidney disease?
questions.explain: Clinical dietitians assess nutritional status and tailor therapeutic diets (such as protein, potassium, and phosphate-controlled regimens in CKD) as well as enteral/parenteral feeds.

open.q: Which healthcare professional designs specialized therapeutic diets and enteral nutrition plans for hospitalized patients?

questions.q: A final-year medical student accidentally administers an extra dose of oral antihypertensive medication to a ward patient. What is the most ethically and professionally appropriate immediate action?
options: Inform supervising staff, monitor the patient and document the error
Conceal the error unless symptoms develop
Delete the medication entry from the chart
Ask the patient not to mention the extra dose
questions.explain: Duty of candour and patient safety require immediate disclosure of medication errors to supervising clinicians so the patient can be closely monitored and managed promptly.

open.q: What ethical duty requires clinicians and students to promptly disclose medical errors to supervising staff and patients?
